basics.name: Chanhyeong Cho
basics.label: Graduate Researcher in Privacy-Enhancing Technologies
basics.summary: Graduate researcher at the Privacy Enhancing Technology Laboratory, Graduate School of Information Security, Korea University. My research focuses on privacy-enhancing technologies, accountable anonymity, anonymous authentication, digital currency security, and privacy for Physical AI. My long-term goal is to develop privacy-preserving security mechanisms that enable safe, private, and accountable coexistence between humans and intelligent machines.

work.name: Privacy Enhancing Technology Laboratory, Korea University
work.summary: Conducting research at the Privacy Enhancing Technology Laboratory in the Graduate School of Information Security, Korea University.
highlights: Researching privacy-enhancing cryptographic protocols, accountable anonymity, and digital currency security.
Designed an accountable anonymous offline electronic cash system supporting selective forward and backward coin tracing.
Studying BBS+ signatures, ElGamal encryption, anonymous credentials, zero-knowledge proofs, accumulators, and revocation mechanisms.
Conducting formal security analysis and implementation-oriented performance evaluation.
Investigating privacy-preserving authentication for robots, autonomous agents, and Industrial Internet of Things environments.
Exploring the protection of visual, audio, biometric, location, and contextual information collected by Physical AI systems.
Studying cryptographically constrained accountability for compromised or malicious autonomous devices.

work.name: Information Security Laboratory, Dankook University
work.summary: Conducted research on privacy-preserving video processing, encrypted data management, and applied information security.
highlights: Designed an entity-specific ROI encryption mechanism supporting selective decryption of surveillance videos.
Developed a post-processing method for protecting facial regions missed by AI-based recognition models.
Participated in the design of an encryption mechanism supporting efficient updates to encrypted cloud data.
Implemented cryptographic and privacy-preserving mechanisms and conducted performance experiments.
Participated in academic conferences, patent development, security competitions, and collaborative research projects.

publications.name: Practical Privacy-Preserving ROI Encryption System for Surveillance Videos Supporting Selective Decryption
publications.publisher: Computer Modeling in Engineering & Sciences, Vol. 141, No. 3
publications.summary: Chanhyeong Cho, Hyun Min Song, and Taek-Young Youn. This work proposes an entity-specific ROI encryption system that selectively decrypts only the target person in surveillance videos while protecting unrelated individuals. It also introduces post-processing to protect facial regions missed by the recognition model.

publications.name: A New Encryption Mechanism Supporting the Update of Encrypted Data for Secure and Efficient Collaboration in the Cloud Environment
publications.publisher: Computer Modeling in Engineering & Sciences, Vol. 142, No. 1
publications.summary: Chanhyeong Cho, Byeori Kim, Haehyun Cho, and Taek-Young Youn. This work proposes a bundled counter-mode encryption mechanism that enables only modified portions of encrypted collaborative data to be updated. The study includes security analysis and experimental evaluation against traditional block cipher modes.

publications.name: Accountable Anonymous Offline Electronic Cash with Selective Coin Tracing
publications.summary: Chanhyeong Cho, Jae Hyun Choi, and Ik Rae Jeong. This work proposes an accountable anonymous offline electronic cash system based on BBS+ signatures and ElGamal encryption. It preserves payer and payee anonymity and transaction unlinkability during normal operation while supporting efficient forward and backward selective coin tracing when illicit activity or double spending is detected.

publications.name: Global Stablecoin Regulations and South Korea's Legislative Landscape: An Analysis of the Impact of Emerging Blockchain Technologies
publications.publisher: KIPS Transactions on Computer and Communication Systems, Accepted
publications.summary: Chanhyeong Cho et al. This study compares major global stablecoin regulatory frameworks with legislative proposals in South Korea. It examines emerging technologies including cross-chain bridges and AI agents and analyzes their implications for privacy, traceability, jurisdiction, and accountability.

portfolio.name: Accountable Anonymous Offline Electronic Cash
portfolio.description: Designed an offline electronic cash protocol providing payer and payee anonymity, transaction unlinkability, and selective forward and backward coin tracing. The protocol uses BBS+ signatures, ElGamal encryption, and zero-knowledge proofs.

portfolio.name: Privacy-Preserving Surveillance Video Encryption
portfolio.description: Developed an entity-specific ROI encryption system supporting selective decryption and privacy protection for facial regions missed by recognition models.

portfolio.name: Dynamic Encrypted Data Update Mechanism
portfolio.description: Designed a bundled counter-mode structure that enables efficient modification of encrypted collaborative data without re-encrypting the complete dataset.

portfolio.name: Privacy-Preserving Authentication and Revocation for IIoT
portfolio.description: Investigating anonymous authentication, revocation, dynamic accumulators, PUF-based key generation, group signatures, and Merkle-tree-based authorization for industrial IoT environments.

portfolio.name: Privacy and Security for Physical AI
portfolio.description: Developing a research framework for privacy-preserving robot authentication, multimodal sensor data protection, controlled disclosure, and accountable autonomous systems. The long-term goal is safe and trustworthy coexistence between humans and robots.

portfolio.name: Stablecoin Regulation and Emerging Blockchain Technologies
portfolio.description: Analyzed global stablecoin regulations, South Korean legislative proposals, cross-chain infrastructure, AI agents, privacy risks, AML and CTF requirements, and technical accountability.
